chunks: And as for what Abu Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ibn Miskan from Walid, the seller of al-Asfat, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked while I was with him about a young girl who had two brothers; the elder married her in Kufa and the younger married her in another land. He said: 'The first [marriage contract] has priority over her, unless the latter has already consummated the marriage with her. If he has consummated it with her, then she is his wife and his marriage is valid.'

The explanation in this report is that when the girl entrusts her affair to both her brothers together, then the elder has priority in contracting the marriage. If both contracts occur at the same time, the contract made by the elder brother has priority, provided that the one who contracted with the younger brother has not yet consummated it. If he has consummated it with her, the contract stands and the elder brother does not have the right to annul it.
ai.seo_question: Who has priority in marriage contract when two brothers marry their sister simultaneously?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *wilayah* (guardianship) in marriage, establishing that when multiple guardians act concurrently, the elder brother holds priority in the initial contract (*aqd*) unless the younger brother’s side consummates the marriage first, thereby validating his claim. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic balance between hierarchical seniority and the legal finality of consummation (*dukhul*), ensuring stability in marital status when competing claims arise.
